overall: The AG found the Council violated the OML by deliberating at a Nov 19, 2024 subcommittee meeting without notice, by approving insufficient minutes for seven meetings, and by posting insufficiently specific notices for Nov 26 and Dec 17 meetings; other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Members allegedly deliberated outside a posted meeting on Oct 15, 2024 while signing Open Meeting Law certificates of receipt.
allegations.key_passage: The act of signing a certification form outside of a meeting is not itself improper deliberation.

allegations.summary: Quorum of Council allegedly deliberated at a Rules and Election Law Subcommittee meeting on Nov 19, 2024 that was not noticed as a joint meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating during the November 19, 2024, meeting without posting notice.

allegations.summary: Minutes of Oct 8, 15, 22 and 29 allegedly failed to list members present; the minutes only said 'Roll Call showed 11 present.'
allegations.key_passage: However, we find the minutes of the October 8, October 15, October 22, and October 29, 2024, meetings to be insufficient where the minutes neither contain a list of the members who were present nor a list of those who were absent.

allegations.summary: Minutes of Nov 5, 12 and 19 listed only absent members rather than present members; allegedly insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by listing in its November 5, November 12 or November 19, 2024, meeting minutes only the members who were absent at each meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes of seven meetings (Oct 8 to Nov 19, 2024) allegedly failed to record each member's roll call vote by name.
allegations.key_passage: Because the minutes of the seven meetings held between October 8 and November 19, 2024, fail to record the roll call votes by documenting the vote of each Council member, we find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the roll call minute violations were intentional; the AG declined to find intent given the prior advisory's context.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we do not find this violation to be intentional.

allegations.summary: Oct 29 minutes allegedly omitted a substitute motion made during discussion of topic 6.9.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the minutes are sufficient as the substitute motion is referenced in the minutes

allegations.summary: Alleged roll call recording failure in a Non-Profit Organizations Subcommittee's Oct 22, 2024 minutes, complaint filed only with the Council.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review the allegation that the Non-Profit Organizations Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to properly record roll call votes

allegations.summary: Alleged insufficiently specific Subcommittee notice for the Nov 19, 2024 meeting; complaint was filed only with the Council.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review this allegation where the complaint was only filed with the Council and not with the Subcommittee.

allegations.summary: Oct 15, 2024 notice allegedly omitted the Certificates as a topic of discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Where a public body does not actually engage in any deliberation on a particular topic, it cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Nov 26 and Dec 17, 2024 executive session notices on OML complaints did not name the complainant.
allegations.key_passage: we find a de minimus violation where the notices did not otherwise identify the specific complaints to be discussed at each meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes of Nov 26 and Dec 17, 2024 allegedly omitted the complainant's name for the OML complaints discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the minutes necessarily do not include the name of the individual who filed the complaints.

allegations.summary: Dec 17, 2024 notice for executive session on Lupoli Companies negotiations did not cite Purpose 6 or reference real property.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the notice of the December 17, 2024, meeting did not reference Purpose 6 or that the discussions pertained to the purchase, exchange, lease or value of real property.

remedy: Amend the minutes of the October 8, October 15, October 22, and October 29, 2024, meetings to include the names of the members who were present.

Amend the minutes of the October 8, October 15, October 22, October 29, November 5, November 12 and November 19, 2024, meetings to record all roll call votes by documenting the vote of each Council member, within thirty days.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order the Council to amend the minutes of the October 8, October 15, October 22, October 29, November 5, November 12 and November 19, 2024, meeting within thirty days of the date of this letter in accordance with the guidance provided above.
